en: The Banaue Rice Terraces act as a giant inclined plane, allowing farmers to walk up the mountain with less effort than climbing straight up.
The Tokay gecko can climb smooth glass walls because microscopic hairs called setae on its toe pads increase friction and molecular attraction.
Galileo famously dropped two spheres of different masses from the Leaning Tower of Pisa to prove gravity accelerates all objects equally.
The Earth acts like a giant bar magnet, which is why the magnetic needle of a compass always points toward the magnetic North Pole.
The Agus River hydroelectric plant in Iligan City generates electricity by using the kinetic energy of flowing water to spin large turbines.
Isaac Newton used a triangular glass prism to prove that white sunlight is actually a mixture of all the colors of the rainbow.
The Philippine pygmy fruit bat uses echolocation, emitting high-frequency sound waves that bounce off objects to help it navigate in the dark.
A Thermos flask keeps soup hot by using a vacuum layer between its walls to prevent heat transfer through conduction and convection.
The human body converts the chemical energy stored in a Lakatan banana into kinetic energy to power muscle movements during physical activities.
The school flagpole uses a simple pulley system, allowing students to easily raise the Philippine flag by pulling down on the rope.
The massive electromagnet in a junkyard crane can lift heavy scrap metal when turned on, but drops it instantly when the electrical current stops.
A drawn longbow stores elastic potential energy, which transforms into the kinetic energy of the arrow the moment the archer releases the string.
